description: Update an existing Security Case Status in OneUptime. Only include the fields you want to change - unspecified fields will remain unchanged. Use get_security_case_status afterwards to see the updated record.

color.description: The status's colour, in hex (#32a852 for example).

description.description: What a case in this status is waiting for, in a sentence.
description.example: This is an example of longer text content that might be stored in this field.

id.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the Security Case Status to update. Required. Use list_security_case_statuses to find IDs.

isAcknowledgedStatus.description: Is it the status a reopened case moves to? From it down, a case counts as taken on. A project has one, and it can't be deleted or archived.

isArchived.description: Archived statuses stay on the cases in them, but can't be picked again. The built-in statuses can't be archived.

isClosedStatus.description: Is it the status Close Case moves a case to? From it down, a case counts as closed and carries a verdict. A project has one.

isContainedStatus.description: Is it the status the time to contain is measured to? From it down, a case counts as contained. A project has one.

isNewStatus.description: Is it the status every new case starts in? A project has one, and it can't be deleted or archived.

name.description: What the status is called, like Investigating or Triage.

order.description: Where this status sits in the project's list of security case statuses: 1 is the top. A case in a status at or below the acknowledged (contained, closed) status counts as acknowledged (contained, closed), so the new, acknowledged, contained and closed statuses have to stay in that order. A new status without a number goes just above the closed status. Setting a number moves the status to that place, and the ones in between shift by one. In the dashboard, drag the rows to reorder them.

name: update_security_case_status
title: Update Security Case Status
